newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA political wing to march in Basque city.
newsitem.headline: ETA political wing to march in Basque city.

text.p: The government of Spain's Basque region granted permission on Thursday for the ETA guerrilla group's political wing to stage a weekend demonstration, despite fears that it might ignite violence.

The authorities had barred a similar march planned for last Saturday because of concerns about a backlash from people outraged by ETA's killing of town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco earlier this month.
On Thursday they said the demonstration, due to start at noon (1000 GMT) on Sunday in San Sebastian, would be allowed to go ahead under heavy security.

ETA's political wing, Herri Batasuna, called the rally in response to anti-ETA marches across Spain last week which drew some six million people, and in a climate where Basques once afraid to speak out now condemn the guerrillas and their allies.
Though most of the marches were peaceful, there were sporadic attacks on Herri Batasuna members and offices.
Herri Batasuna's past demonstrations have sometimes ended in confrontations with police and there were concerns that any pro-ETA gathering might bring further violence.

ETA on Wednesday formally claimed responsibility for Blanco's killing. He was kidnapped on July 10 and shot in the head two days later after the government refused ETA's demand to transfer 500 of its prisoners to the Basque region.

"ETA assumes and will assume in the future, with its head held high, the consequences of the conflict as crude and painful as they may be," the group said in a statement published in the radical newspaper EGIN, its usual mouthpiece.
Euskadi Ta Askatasuna (ETA), or Basque Homeland and Freedom, has killed more than 800 people in nearly 30 years of fighting for an independent Basque state.
A forum of political parties in the Basque region known as Ajuria Enea was to meet on Thursday to assess the situation after Blanco's death.
Ajuria Enea comprises all the region's parties except Herri Batasuna. At its last meeting on July 13, the day Blanco died, the forum vowed to isolate Herri Batasuna.
The leading political forces in the region put that policy into action last week by launching a bid to vote out one of Herri Batasuna's most influential mayors, in the town of Mondragon.
The central government in Madrid also embraced the isolation policy and proposed a crackdown on street violence, some types of demonstrations and any actions construed as "defence of terrorism".
Herri Batasuna holds two seats in the national congress. In the most recent elections in the Basque region, it received about 15 percent of the vote.
